name: Pixar-Style IP Brand Ad Short
description: Develops an IP character description, brand/prop settings, an ad storyline or reference assets into a Pixar 3D cartoon style brand ad short, advancing in stages through character attribute locking, prop anchoring, storyboard planning, video clip generation and audio composition, ensuring consistency of the character, prop, storyboard and video reference chain.

planning.planning_notes:
[Interactive progressive information gathering]
Gate 1: confirm the brand name, product category, character archetype and aspect ratio.
Gate 2: confirm the target duration, narrative tone and dialogue needs.
Gate 3: confirm the character attribute table, containing at least color, body type, eyes, body appendages such as ears/horns/wings/tail, occupational markers, clothing accessories and key exclusions; if the user chooses a preset character, give 4 complete attribute options + a custom option.
Gate 4: enter prop anchoring only after the character attributes are locked, distinguishing product props from character-related props.
Gate 5: offer 3 narrative frameworks to choose from: discovery structure, challenge structure, vision structure, and allow a custom one.
Gate 6: integrate the brand, character, props, narrative, aspect ratio, tone and audio needs into a style lock card and a scene outline.

[Execution path]
1. After the character attributes are locked, generate the ad IP character anchor portrait; the character anchor must be a source node that does not reference the character itself, and prop anchoring begins after the character anchor is complete.
2. The prop anchoring stage distinguishes product props from character-related props: product props are shown independently, and character-related props must reference the character anchor; multiple props can run in parallel.
3. Based on the character anchor, the prop anchors and the narrative framework, generate the storyboard plan, organized as Sequence → Shot Group → Shot, and make the storyboard plan clear and reviewable.
4. Split and generate video clips according to the storyboard plan. A 15-second ad is usually split into 4 video clips; a 30-second ad usually into 6 video clips; a single clip does not exceed 8 seconds.
5. Generate the audio layers only after all video clips are complete, including background music, sound effects, narration or voiceover; video clips by default write only sound effects (in the same language as the dialogue) and do not mix in BGM ahead of time.
6. After all video clips and audio layers are complete, final editing, mixing and export are handled by the canvas compose node.

[Panel count formula]
15-second ad = 9 panels; 30-second ad = 12-15 panels; 60-second ad = 18-24 panels.
The aspect ratio confirmed before starting must run through all image and video stages.
planning.prompt_guide:
Write all prompts in the same language as the user's input.

[Pixar visual language]
Pixar 3D cartoon rendering, C4D + Octane texture, rounded character modeling, delicate plush or smooth materials, soft warm-orange lighting, bright, approachable and commercial-ad-friendly overall; avoid realism, horror, cyberpunk, ink-wash, gloomy gray or adult-looking textures.

[Anchor picture style]
Character and prop anchors use a minimal light beige or light gray solid background, with the subject complete and edges clear, convenient for cutout and downstream referencing; the logo and brand text must be clearly readable.

[Storyboard and video style]
Storyboard sketches stay black-and-white pencil line drawings, without color or grayscale; video clips continue the same Pixar cartoon look, warm natural light, rounded character proportions and ad-grade clean composition.

[Cross-stage expression]
Character prompts must contain the complete attribute table and "Character look lock: ..., later nodes must not change it"; downstream prompts must quote the character's core features, the prop anchors and the brand name verbatim, keeping the tone unified and the shot descriptions specific.
conduct_rules: Collect information in the order of the gates; do not ask about later complex details before the basic creative identity is confirmed
Do not generate the character anchor before the character attribute table is complete
The character portrait must be a source node that does not reference the character itself; only after the character portrait is complete may the prop anchor and storyboard sketch stages begin
Execute strictly in the order character portrait → prop anchors → storyboard sketches → video clips → audio layers → final composition, without skipping steps
Each stage creates only its corresponding nodes; do not merge the character, props, storyboard, video and audio into one output
Prop anchors must distinguish product props from character-related props: product props are shown independently, and character-related props must reference the character anchor
Prop anchors and the storyboard plan must take the character portrait as reference input.
Props by default prioritize clear structure and brand legibility; only make a multi-angle display when the user explicitly chooses multi-angle
The storyboard plan must contain numbering, time range, shot goal, action, scene, prop appearance timing and the final brand/product lock frame.
Enter the video stage only after the storyboard planning stage is complete.
Shot-by-shot videos must use the confirmed storyboard as storyboard guidance while referencing the character portrait and the prop anchors.
Video clips may be generated in parallel, but each clip must be bound to a continuous range of storyboard panels, with a single clip not exceeding 8 seconds
Each video must keep the complete reference chain of the character portrait, prop anchors and storyboard sketches, without breaks
Video prompts must contain the character look lock and the constraint that the protagonist is not duplicated
Sound effects in video clip prompts must be described in the same language as the dialogue, with no background music made explicit
The audio layers are generated after all video clips are complete; do not mix BGM into the video clips ahead of time
Final composition is handled by the canvas compose node.
Final composition accepts only video and audio outputs; text, briefs or prompts must not be used as media input
The character's core features (fur color, body type, ears, expression, etc.) must be quoted verbatim and locked in all downstream node prompts
The brand name and product selling points must not be rewritten or omitted in storyboard and video prompts
When the user modifies the character, regenerate the character anchor and cascade-update the props, storyboards and videos that reference it
When the user modifies a prop, regenerate only the prop anchor and the video clips that reference that prop
When the user modifies the storyboard, regenerate only the affected panels and the corresponding video clips, without rerunning the entire flow

rating_bands.description: Character/prop/storyboard/video styles are highly unified, brand elements are clear, and the narrative is smooth and complete
The style is basically unified, with occasional detail deviations that do not affect the overall look
Obvious style inconsistency, character/prop deformation or missing brand elements
The character/props deviate seriously from the settings, the storyboard and video do not correspond, and it is unusable

visual_review_items.name: Character consistency
visual_review_items.description: The character's look is consistent across the portrait, props, storyboard and video

visual_review_items.name: Prop consistency
visual_review_items.description: Prop appearance matches the anchor image, and brand text is clear

visual_review_items.name: Style unity
visual_review_items.description: Pixar 3D cartoon rendering, soft warm tones and rounded modeling style are unified

visual_review_items.name: Storyboard quality
visual_review_items.description: Storyboard composition is clear, action directions are explicit, and shot language is sound

text_review_items.name: Narrative completeness
text_review_items.description: Whether the storyboard plot covers the ad narrative arc (introduction → discovery → climax → ending)

text_review_items.name: Brand information accuracy
text_review_items.description: Whether the brand name, slogan and product selling points are embedded accurately

text_review_items.name: Prompt structure quality
text_review_items.description: Whether the shot-by-shot prompts contain character lock, prop references, scene and performance instructions

text_review_items.name: Audio and composition readiness
text_review_items.description: Whether the audio layers cover all video clips and can be aligned with the video outputs for composition

domain_constraints: The character's look is locked throughout and its core features must not change in the storyboard/video/composition stages
Prop appearance must strictly match the prop anchors, without deformation, added irrelevant details or altered brand spelling
The storyboard plan must cover the ad narrative arc, brand/product display and the final closing frame
Video clips must refer to the corresponding shot actions and compositions of the confirmed storyboard
Each video must reference the character portrait and, as needed, the relevant prop anchors, with the reference chain unbroken
The protagonist appears only once in each video shot, with no duplicated characters or clones
The brand logo display must match the prop anchor, with clearly readable text
